text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- New Suez-Lyonnaise des Eaux group to be created in June aims for the first global ranking in local services to municipalities.
-- Merger of Dassault Aviation and Aerospatiale may be effective this summer, to be followed by a privatisation before end 1997.
-- Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier wants Belgian businessman Albert Frere to choose between Canal Plus and CLT and wishes CLT sells its stake in digital-TV service TPS.
-- Government seeks to limit to 0.75 percent the rise of government spending for 1998 budget.

-- Legrand chairman Francois Grappotte says in an interview he does not believe that shorter work hours are an answer to unemployment, adds state must not restrict companies from developing, since growth is the way out of unemployment.
-- Government seeks to restructure film producer SFP before privatisation.

-- Lyonnaise des Eaux vice-chairman Guy de Panafieu says in an interview the new company's treasury reserves will total four billion francs, adds cash pile will allow it to proceed with projects without incurring debt.

-- Schneider chairman Didier Pineau Valencienne says in an interview group does not rule out buying companies in electric wiring and industrial control systems, as well as automation, seeks to increase international activity notably in Asia, adds considers buying out company shares to protect net profit per share.
-- Unemployed peaople from all over Europe to demonstrate in Amsterdam on June 14 for joint European action against unemeployment.
-- EBRD holds annual meeting in London today.
